name: IBM color-blind safe
summary: Five colors from IBM Design Language's color-blind safe palette: ultramarine, indigo, magenta, orange and gold.
guidance: IBM publishes this five-color set so charts and status colors can be told apart by people with color blindness.
It has no green. If you need a success color, use the info blue or a checkmark icon with a text label rather than adding a green that blends with the orange.
Built for color-blind accessibility: the hues stay distinguishable for the most common types of color blindness, mainly by differing in lightness as well as hue.
Several of these colors are too light to carry white text. Put dark text (ink) on them, as the contrast checks below show, and never white text.
Body text needs 4.5:1 against its background; large text and UI outlines need 3:1.
Still pair every status color with an icon or text. Color alone should never be the only signal.

credit.text: IBM Design Language, Color blind safe palette (data visualization). The hex values are the published palette.
